The MCU supply pins are not on the +3V3 rail or on +3.3V. The +3.3V net (LDO REG1 OUT) and the +3V3 net that feeds the MCU pull-ups and decoupling are never joined by any component.",
      "expected": "Spec: the 3V3 LDO (REG1) 'produces 3V3 for MCUs and Sensors', and 3V3 'feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC)'. Every MCU VDD/VDDA pin should be tied to the 3.3 V supply, and the LDO output rail should reach the MCU rail.",

        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"216\") (name \"unconnected-(FCC2-VDD-Pad11)\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"FCC2\") (pin \"11\") (pinfunction \"VDD\") (pintype \"power_in\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"1\") (name \"+3.3V\") (class \"Default\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"2\") (name \"+3V3\") (class \"Default\")"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "3.3 V LDO (MCUs + sensors) | Hades (top sheet) | ST LD39200PU33R"}
      ],
      "impact": "If these pins are truly unconnected, neither MCU receives supply and the flight computer and navigation computer cannot run. Even if the export has lost labels, the netlist as given does not connect the MCUs to power.",

    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["NAVC2"],
      "pins": ["NAVC2.18", "NAVC2.63", "NAVC2.12"],
      "nets": ["Net-(NAVC2-VSS-Pad18)", "unconnected-(NAVC2-VSSA-Pad12)", "GND"],
      "observed": "NAVC2 VSS pins 18 and 63 are on a generated net 'Net-(NAVC2-VSS-Pad18)' that contains only those two pins. NAVC2 is absent from the GND net, and VSSA pin 12 is isolated. The FCC2 ground pins are on GND, but the NAVC2 ground pins are not.",
      "expected": "All VSS and VSSA pins of the STM32F405 should be tied to the GND net, as the FCC2 VSS pins are.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"144\") (name \"Net-(NAVC2-VSS-Pad18)\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"NAVC2\") (pin \"18\") (pinfunction \"VSS\") (pintype \"power_in\")) (node (ref \"NAVC2\") (pin \"63\") (pinfunction \"VSS\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"FCC2\") (pin \"10\") (pinfunction \"VSS\") (pintype \"power_in\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The navigation MCU would have no ground reference, so it cannot operate and its peripherals and sensors would have no return path.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist leaves the MCU supply and ground pins isolated: the VDD/VDDA pins of both MCUs are on single-pin nets, the +3.3V LDO rail and the +3V3 MCU rail are never joined, and NAVC2's VSS pins are off GND. These are real connectivity gaps, though the export may have lost labels, so confidence is moderate."
}

anomalies.observed: All VDD pins of both MCUs (NAVC2 pins 19, 32, 48, 64; FCC2 pins 11, 27, 50, 75, 100) sit on single-pin nets. FCC2 VDDA and VBAT are also isolated. The MCU supply pins are not on the +3V3 rail or on +3.3V. The +3.3V net (LDO REG1 OUT) and the +3V3 net that feeds the MCU pull-ups and decoupling are never joined by any component.
anomalies.expected: Spec: the 3V3 LDO (REG1) 'produces 3V3 for MCUs and Sensors', and 3V3 'feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC)'. Every MCU VDD/VDDA pin should be tied to the 3.3 V supply, and the LDO output rail should reach the MCU rail.

evidence.quote: 3.3 V LDO (MCUs + sensors) | Hades (top sheet) | ST LD39200PU33R

anomalies.impact: If these pins are truly unconnected, neither MCU receives supply and the flight computer and navigation computer cannot run. Even if the export has lost labels, the netlist as given does not connect the MCUs to power.

anomalies.observed: NAVC2 VSS pins 18 and 63 are on a generated net 'Net-(NAVC2-VSS-Pad18)' that contains only those two pins. NAVC2 is absent from the GND net, and VSSA pin 12 is isolated. The FCC2 ground pins are on GND, but the NAVC2 ground pins are not.
anomalies.expected: All VSS and VSSA pins of the STM32F405 should be tied to the GND net, as the FCC2 VSS pins are.
anomalies.impact: The navigation MCU would have no ground reference, so it cannot operate and its peripherals and sensors would have no return path.

These are real connectivity gaps, though the export may have lost labels, so confidence is moderate.
